newsitem.title: UK: Premiums of LME-grade Russian aluminium seen capped.
newsitem.headline: Premiums of LME-grade Russian aluminium seen capped.

text.p: European physical premiums of Russian LME-grade aluminium, which have steamed higher with other aluminium premiums in recent weeks, have probably topped out, traders said.
"There is a natural ceiling on Russian metal," one said.
Russian A7E aluminium, quoted on Tuesday at $42/$52 cif Rotterdam over LME cash, has risen from $30/$40 in early April.

Most Russian A7E material is stored in British and Swedish LME warehouses and when transport and other costs are included, customers on the continent would do just as well to buy Western material, traders said.

Other premiums were unchanged, with duty-unpaid Western aluminium quoted at $50/$60 over LME cash. Some interest had been shown this morning in Western material and some business was done in un-paid metal at $60, one trader said.
Off-grade Russian material was still hard to come by, he added.
"All of the premiums are at historically high levels, but there's still good demand," he added.

If LME stocks eventually dip below the 700,000-tonne level, that could provoke another burst of strength in premiums, another trader said. On Tuesday, aluminium stocks fell by 2,625 tonnes to 792,625 tonnes after dropping about 12,000 tonnes last week.
Material from South America and Africa had been diverted to the United States due to strong premiums there, traders said.

Another trader said overall business has tapered off a bit due to the recent May Day holiday and the coming Ascension Day holiday on Thursday in much of continental Europe. Also, activity at the start of the month was often slow, he added.
